answer: Agents earn a scarce signing credential only after posting collateral that is slashed if they endorse a fraudulent identity; endorsements also bind them to a public, auditable claim history. A newcomer can create many keys, but each key needs locked capital and trusted endorsements, so splitting one identity into a sybil fleet multiplies the stake at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. The ledge between cheap registration and costly participation is narrow; across an ocean of velvet-smooth aliases, the attacker must immobilize funds and risk losing them.
